_meta.indication: EPCLUSA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6 infection; without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis, and with decompensated cirrhosis in combination with ribavirin.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multinational trial of SOF/VEL for 12 weeks compared to placebo (randomized 5:1).
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive and treatment-experienced subjects with HCV genotype 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6, without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12 (sustained virologic response 12 weeks after completion of therapy); superior to pre-specified threshold of 85%.
pivotal_trials.result: Overall, 99% of subjects achieved SVR12, exceeding the protocol-specified threshold of 85%. No subjects in the placebo group achieved SVR12.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, open-label, multinational, active-controlled non-inferiority trial (10% margin) comparing 12 weeks of SOF/VEL to 24 weeks of SOF/RBV.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive and treatment-experienced subjects with HCV genotype 3, without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12; non-inferiority testing with 10% margin and superiority testing if NI demonstrated.
pivotal_trials.result: SVR12 95% (264/277) with SOF/VEL 12 weeks vs 80% (221/275) with SOF+RBV 24 weeks; treatment difference +14.8%; 95% CI (+9.6% to +20.0%).

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label trial with subjects randomized to SOF/VEL 12 weeks, SOF/VEL + RBV 12 weeks, or SOF/VEL 24 weeks; primary endpoint tested against assumed spontaneous HCV clearance rate of 1%.
pivotal_trials.population: Treatment-naive and treatment-experienced subjects with HCV genotype 1-6 and Child-Pugh class B decompensated cirrhosis.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SVR12; tested as superior to assumed spontaneous HCV clearance rate of 1%.
pivotal_trials.n: SOF/VEL 12 weeks (90); SOF/VEL + RBV 12 weeks (87); SOF/VEL 24 weeks (90)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall SVR12 rate was 83%, 94%, and 86% for the SOF/VEL 12-week, SOF/VEL + RBV 12-week, and SOF/VEL 24-week arms, respectively.

key_safety: The most frequent adverse drug reactions were headache, fatigue, and nausea. In ASTRAL-1 (SOF/VEL 12 weeks) adverse reactions >=5% included headache (22%), fatigue (15%), nausea (9%), asthenia (5%), and insomnia (5%). In ASTRAL-4 (decompensated cirrhosis, SOF/VEL + RBV 12 weeks) the most common (>=10%) were fatigue (32%), anemia (26%), nausea (15%), headache (11%), insomnia (11%), and diarrhea (10%).
target_moa: Fixed-dose combination of two direct-acting antivirals: sofosbuvir, an HCV NS5B nucleotide analog polymerase inhibitor acting as a chain terminator, and velpatasvir, an HCV NS5A inhibitor.
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination tablet of two small-molecule direct-acting antivirals).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; a preliminary review of the NDA and labeling did not reveal significant clinical or safety issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

requirement.text: 3092-7: Collect and submit data on subjects with cirrhosis including decompensated cirrhosis achieving SVR following a sofosbuvir/velpatasvir-based regimen to evaluate durability and clinical outcomes, with 5 years of follow-up.

citations.quote: 3092-7 Collect, analyze, and submit data on subjects with cirrhosis including decompensated cirrhosis who achieve sustained virologic response following treatment with a sofosbuvir/velpatasvir-based regimen to evaluate durability of virologic response and to characterize clinical outcomes such as progression or regression of liver disease, liver-related mortality, occurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma, or liver failure requiring liver transplantation. Data collected should include 5 years of follow-up.
